title: Binomial Theorem: Pascal's Triangle, Expansions and Coefficients
seo_title: Binomial Theorem Class 11 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_text: Historical perspective, statement and proof of the binomial theorem for positive integral indices; Pascal's triangle; simple applications (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 11 Binomial Theorem worksheet (NCERT Chapter 7): Pascal's triangle, ⁿCᵣ, number of terms, expansions, coefficients, sum of coefficients and evaluating powers like 99⁴. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: (a + b)ⁿ = Σ ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ, with n + 1 terms.
key_sub: The coefficients are row n of Pascal's triangle.
body_html:
How it works

  • (a + b)n = nC0an + nC1an−1b + … + nCnbn; there are n + 1 terms.
  • The coefficients are row n of Pascal's triangle: 1, 4, 6, 4, 1 for n = 4.
  • In (a − b)n the signs alternate. Put x = 1 to find the sum of the coefficients.
  • Powers like 994 = (100 − 1)4 can be found term by term.
Example

Expand (x + 2)4.

1, 4, 6, 4, 1 are the coefficients

x⁴ + 4·2x³ + 6·4x² + 4·8x + 16

Answer: x⁴ + 8x³ + 24x² + 32x + 16

Common mistakes

  • Writing (a + b)ⁿ = aⁿ + bⁿ.
  • Counting n terms instead of n + 1.
  • Forgetting to raise the number in the bracket to its power.

faq.q: How many terms does (a + b)ⁿ have?
What is the sum of the numbers in row n of Pascal's triangle?

items.q: How many terms are in the expansion of (x + y)7?
items.e: The powers of x go from 7 down to 0, which is 8 terms.

items.q: What is the coefficient of x²y⁶ in the expansion of (x + y)8?
items.e: The term is 8C6 x²y⁶, and 8C6 = 28.

items.q: Find <sup>10</sup>C<sub>8</sub>.
items.e: 10C8 = 10! / (8! · 2!) = 45. It is entry 8 in row 10 of Pascal's triangle (starting from 0).

items.q: Which list is row 7 of Pascal's triangle (the row that starts 1, 7)?
items.e: Each entry is nCk, the sum of the two entries above it. 1, 7, 21, 35, 35, 21, 7, 1.

items.q: What is the coefficient of x7y² in the expansion of (x + y)9?
items.e: The term is 9C2 x7y², and 9C2 = 36.

items.q: What is the coefficient of x²y⁴ in the expansion of (x + y)6?
items.e: The term is 6C4 x²y⁴, and 6C4 = 15.

items.q: Find <sup>8</sup>C<sub>7</sub>.
items.e: 8C7 = 8! / (7! · 1!) = 8. It is entry 7 in row 8 of Pascal's triangle (starting from 0).

items.q: Find <sup>4</sup>C<sub>2</sub>.

items.q: Find <sup>4</sup>C<sub>3</sub>.

items.q: Which list is row 4 of Pascal's triangle (the row that starts 1, 4)?

items.q: In the expansion of (x + y)5, what is the sum of the exponents in each term?
c: It changes from term to term
items.e: In each term xayb, a + b = 5.

items.q: What is the coefficient of xy³ in the expansion of (x + y)4?
items.e: The term is 4C3 xy³, and 4C3 = 4.

items.q: Expand (3x − 1)3.
items.e: Use row 3 of Pascal's triangle (1, 3, 3, 1) with powers of 3x going down and powers of −1 going up. 27x³ − 27x² + 9x − 1.

items.q: Expand (x − 3)4.
items.e: Use row 4 of Pascal's triangle (1, 4, 6, 4, 1) with powers of x going down and powers of −3 going up. x⁴ − 12x³ + 54x² − 108x + 81.

items.q: Expand (x + 2)2.
items.e: Use row 2 of Pascal's triangle (1, 2, 1) with powers of x going down and powers of 2 going up. x² + 4x + 4.

items.q: What is the coefficient of x² in the expansion of (3x − 3)6?
items.e: The term with x² is 6C4(3x)2(−3)4 = 15 · 9 · 81 = 10,935x².

items.q: Use the binomial theorem to evaluate 11<sup>3</sup>.
items.e: (10 + 1)3 = 3C0·103·(1) + 3C1·102·(1) + 3C2·101·(1)2 + 3C3·(1)3 (add all 4 terms, not only the first and the last). So 113 = 1,331.

items.q: Use the binomial theorem to evaluate 1001<sup>3</sup>.
items.e: (1000 + 1)3 = 3C0·10003·(1) + 3C1·10002·(1) + 3C2·10001·(1)2 + 3C3·(1)3 (add all 4 terms, not only the first and the last). So 10013 = 1,00,30,03,001.

items.q: Use the binomial theorem to evaluate 999<sup>3</sup>.
items.e: (1000 − 1)3 = 3C0·10003·(−1) + 3C1·10002·(−1) + 3C2·10001·(−1)2 + 3C3·(−1)3 (add all 4 terms, not only the first and the last). So 9993 = 99,70,02,999.
